title: Best Time to Buy and Sell
statement:
You know a stock's price on each of `n` days. Buy one share on one day and sell it on a later day, and find the most profit you can make.

The first line is the number of days `n`, at least 1. The second line has the `n` prices in order, whole numbers of 0 or more separated by spaces. Print the largest profit, the sell price minus the buy price, where you buy before you sell. When no trade makes money, for example when the prices only fall or there is only one day, print `0`.

Input:

```text
6
7 1 5 3 6 4
```

Expected output:

```text
5
```

Buying at `1` on the second day and selling at `6` on the fifth day makes `5`.
hints: Checking every pair of days works but is slow. One pass is enough if you remember the right thing from the days behind you.
Selling today, the best day to have bought was the cheapest day so far. Keep the lowest price so far and the best profit so far.
On each day, update the lowest price, then see whether selling today at today's price beats the best profit.

python.solution:
def max_profit(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    lowest = prices[0]  # the cheapest price so far
    best = 0
    for price in prices:
        lowest = min(lowest, price)
        best = max(best, price - lowest)
    return best


n = int(input())
prices = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print(max_profit(prices))
